report.source_text: Intraoperatively the patient was kept on left side 20° with an incision done in the right nostril, the mucosa was separated and the sphenoid sinus mucosa removed. The sellar floor identified and removed. Thick capsule of abscess incised with yellowish pus was drained. The cavity was cleaned and irrigated with antibiotics and saline. The pus was sent for Gram stain, culture, acid-fast bacilli (AFB) stain and histopathological evaluation. The pituitary was not removed.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old Bahraini male presented to the emergency department in March 2016 with a one-month history of progressive severe headache exacerbated by bright light, photosensitivity, nausea, left eye blurred vision, and generalized fatigue. MRI brain on admission revealed a heterogeneously hyperintense lesion on T2-weighted images with peripheral hypointensity and a fluid level on T1 images, located in the sellar region with optic chiasm compression and displacement superiorly, and mild cavernous sinus compression. These imaging findings were consistent with a sellar mass lesion. The patient underwent transsphenoidal drainage in July 2016, which revealed a thick abscess capsule with yellowish pus, confirming the diagnosis of pituitary abscess. Gram stain showed few WBC with sterile culture and negative AFB stain. Histopathology confirmed features suggestive of an inflammatory lesion consistent with abscess, with no evidence of pituitary adenoma. Postoperatively, the patient received broad-spectrum antibiotics (metronidazole 400 mg three times daily, ceftriaxone 1 g once daily, and vancomycin 1 g twice daily) for 6 weeks. Follow-up MRI demonstrated complete resolution of the abscess with no enhancing residual pockets within the pituitary fossa. The patient showed clinical improvement with normal functional status.
